# Build For Good

> Build For Good is a global, multidisciplinary community for turning meaningful problems into collective action — exceptional people across every field, building things that matter, together.

Build For Good (BFG) brings together genuine, ambitious, curious and compassionate people who want to become more capable without becoming less human. It is deliberately multidisciplinary — engineering, medicine, science, design, law, policy, philosophy and the skilled trades meet on real work rather than in name.

It is **open to problems and selective with people**: anyone, anywhere can submit a problem through the Problem Commons, while membership is earned through an application, a short conversation and a 30-day trial. Membership is judged by conduct, not credentials.

- Motto: **Build. Grow. Evolve. Together.**
- Founder & Steward: Nikhil Nagpure — Build For Good belongs to its members, not to any one founder's company.
- How to bring a problem: submit one at <https://buildforgood.world/problems#submit>. No membership required. Every submission is framed, parked, or declined with a reason, and gets a human answer within 72 hours.
- How to apply to join: apply at <https://buildforgood.world/membership#apply>. Application → a 15–20 minute voice conversation → a 30-day provisional trial. No CV and no years-of-experience field, by design.
- The standard: twelve dimensions of character and capability, with **Character as a gate** rather than an average (a 1–2 on Character is declined regardless of other scores; otherwise Character ≥ 4 and the average of the rest ≥ 3).
- Rituals: five recurring formats — Build Night, Deep Dive, Challenge, Think and Impact — plus quarterly rhythms (Showcase, Retreat/Meetup, Charter Review, Project Retros, New Member Cohort).
- Contact: hello@buildforgood.world — a person reads every message, usually within 72 hours.

## Pages

- [Home](https://buildforgood.world/): What Build For Good is, who it is for, and the three doors into it — bring a problem, apply to join, or join a Lab.
- [Manifesto](https://buildforgood.world/manifesto): Why Build For Good exists — capability without character is not enough — plus what we build, what we refuse to be, and the standard members hold each other to.
- [Values](https://buildforgood.world/values): The eight values, each written twice as the behaviour the community rewards and the behaviour it corrects.
- [Membership](https://buildforgood.world/membership): The filter — the twelve dimensions, a real conversation, and a 30-day trial. How to apply to join.
- [Problem Commons](https://buildforgood.world/problems): Submit a problem from anywhere, no membership required; problems are framed, parked or declined with a reason, and can become Labs.
- [Projects](https://buildforgood.world/projects): The member-submitted, human-reviewed showcase of what the community is building, at every stage from idea to scaled.
- [Activities](https://buildforgood.world/activities): The five recurring rituals — Build Night, Deep Dive, Challenge, Think and Impact — and the quarterly rhythm.
- [About](https://buildforgood.world/about): What the name means (Build, Grow, Evolve, Together), the multidisciplinary design, and the North Star: become more capable without becoming less human.
- [Founders & Stewards](https://buildforgood.world/founders): The people who started and steward Build For Good, and what each role owns. No invented team, no borrowed titles.
- [Contact](https://buildforgood.world/contact): Message the team, suggest an idea, or report a problem. A human usually replies within 72 hours.
- [Privacy](https://buildforgood.world/privacy): Privacy policy for the Build For Good website.
- [Terms](https://buildforgood.world/terms): Terms of use for the Build For Good website.
- [Accessibility](https://buildforgood.world/accessibility): Accessibility statement for the Build For Good website.

## Optional

- [GitHub](https://github.com/webuildforgood): Open-source code and issue tracker for the Build For Good community platform.

- [Contact](mailto:hello@buildforgood.world): Email the team directly.
